Kyle Hawkins

Republican candidate for Supreme Court, Place 7, Texas

Justice, Supreme Court of Texas (Place 7); attorney

Kyle Hawkins is a Republican who has served as Justice of the Supreme Court of Texas, Place 7, since Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him in October 2025 to replace Justice Jeffrey S. Boyd. He was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. He is running for a full term against Democrat Kristen Hawkins (no relation) in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Hawkins stands

Judicial philosophy
Says the job of a judge is to "uphold the rule of law by applying the law as written without fear or favor" (from a Bloomberg Law interview quoted by the Dallas Morning News).
2020 election lawsuit
While serving as Texas Solicitor General, he did not sign Attorney General Ken Paxton's lawsuit challenging the 2020 presidential election results.

Background

  • Justice, Supreme Court of Texas, Place 7 (appointed Oct. 24, 2025; took office Oct. 27, 2025)
  • Counselor to the U.S. Solicitor General, U.S. Department of Justice transition team (2025)
  • Texas Solicitor General (2018–2021)
  • Texas Assistant Solicitor General (2017–2018)
  • Attorney in private practice at Lehotsky Keller and Gibson Dunn
  • Law clerk to Justice Samuel Alito, U.S. Supreme Court, and Judge Edith Jones, U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit
  • J.D., University of Minnesota Law School (2009)
